stories.headline: Pearsall's Season Dies on the Table, and Deebo Rides Back Into Town Same Afternoon
stories.read: Lynch stepped to the porch Saturday and said it plain: Pearsall needs a knee rebuilt, six to twelve months, the whole 2026 haul gone. Before the dust settled San Francisco had Deebo Samuel signed back on a one-year handshake worth seven million, and Christian Kirk's laid up with a bad calf besides. Here's the read, pardner. Somebody in that wagon has to catch a hundred-odd throws and the pecking order at that ranch just got shorter than a Sunday sermon. Deebo's cheap as day-old coffee in the great land grab and he's walkin' into a room with nobody left standin' in front of him. That's the vein. Go pan it before your outfit hears the news.

stories.headline: Bijan and Gibbs Sit on the Fence Rail While the Whole Saloon Sweats
stories.read: Two of the finest ball-carriers in the territory have reported to camp and refused to take a single rep, both waitin' on the money men to open the strongbox. Gibbs has now watched four straight practices in a hoodie. Robinson piled up 2,298 all-purpose yards last season and aims to be the highest-paid runner alive when the ink dries. Doc has seen this hand before and it always folds the same way: these fellas are holdin' IN, not holdin' out, which means they get paid and they play. Every nervous greenhorn in your outfit is quietly slidin' 'em down the board. Let 'em. You sit tight at the top of the great land grab and take a bell-cow a half-round cheaper than he's worth.

stories.headline: Stefon Diggs Still Wanderin' the Open Range, and Five Outfits Are Circlin'
stories.read: Camp's rollin' and one of the better route-runners in the game still ain't got a bunkhouse. Fowler says Washington's the interestin' fit and Schefter reckons the feelin' runs both ways, with at least five clubs kickin' the tires. Now listen close: a fella with no ranch has no draft price, which means the saloon has plumb forgotten he exists. The second he signs somewhere with thin receivin' help, his worth doubles overnight and everybody scrambles. Doc says stash the last pick of your bench on him if the ink dries before your land grab, and if it don't, be the first hand to stake that claim on the open range come September.
